target.title: feat(release): add monthly npm stable publication
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw cannot currently publish a trailing-month core package to the npm `stable` dist-tag without either treating it like a regular `latest` release or adopting the much larger superseded release-policy framework. The existing Full Release Validation graph also rejects the required `stable/YYYY.M.33` workflow ref, making a guarded monthly stable run unreachable.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one npm-only stable mode to the existing release workflow. Final `YYYY.M.PATCH` versions at patch `33` or later must publish from the exact `stable/YYYY.M.33` branch, with the release tag, checkout, branch tip, package version, preflight run, Full Release Validation run, manifest, and promoted tarball all bound to the same commit.

The implementation reuses the existing preflight manifest v1 and tested tarball, captures the prior npm `stable` selector before mutation, performs bounded exact-version and selector readback, and records a selector-only repair command. Full Release Validation now narrowly trusts the canonical stable branch shape and verifies every required child run used the target SHA. Plugin publication, native platforms, GitHub Releases, private dist-tags, Docker, mobile, and website publication remain out of scope.

Protected `main` must be on any strictly later calendar month with a daily patch below `33`, so supported maintenance patches remain publishable after development advances more than one month.

Fork and non-production rehearsals can explicitly set `bypass_stable_guard=true` to relax the `.33` threshold and protected-`main` month policy. The bypass is stable-only and default-off; it still requires the canonical stable branch, branch-tip/tag/checkout SHA equality, final tag/package identity, authenticated validation evidence, the verified tarball, environment approval, and registry proof.

## User Impact

Release operators can publish the completed month's core `openclaw` package to npm `stable`, beginning at `.33`, without moving `latest` or invoking other publication surfaces. Maintainers can exercise the same guarded path with a historical test version by enabling the audited bypass. Existing user-facing `stable | beta | dev` CLI channel behavior is unchanged by this PR; the CLI/channel migration remains separate work.

## Evidence

- Focused Vitest: 6 files, 199 tests passed.
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs`: passed, including zizmor and direct-input interpolation checks.
- Focused oxlint and formatting checks: passed.
- Core test TypeScript check: passed.
- `node --check scripts/openclaw-npm-stable-release.mjs`: passed.
- `bash -n scripts/openclaw-npm-publish.sh`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent code, dead-code, documentation, and Full Validation reachability reviews found no remaining blocker or major issue.

## Manual Validation

- Verified the real release-check trusted-ref shell guard accepts `stable/2026.6.33` and `stable/2026.12.33` while rejecting zero-padded, out-of-range, wrong-patch, suffixed, and arbitrary stable refs.
- Verified the workflow contract dispatches CI, plugin prerelease, release checks, and performance from the stable workflow ref with the resolved target SHA, and fails closed if a required child head SHA differs.
- Verified `bypass_stable_guard` is rejected for non-stable tags and malformed values, preserves canonical branch and release identity, and relaxes only patch/month eligibility.
- Live stable preflight, environment approval, npm publication, and registry readback are intentionally pending; this PR does not claim production publication proof.
